alia, containing the Notice of the AGM.  The same is also available on the Company’s website at

mail Ids are registered with the Company/ Depositories. Furt her, a physical letter providing the web -

Empowering a
Greener 
Bharat
India's renewable energy ambitions are transforming 
the country's power landscape at an unprecedented 
pace. The true success of this transformation 
depends not only on creating renewable assets, but 
also on ensuring that they continue to perform with 
reliability, efficiency and consistency throughout 
their operating life. As India’s renewable footprint 
grows in both scale and complexity, O&M (operations 
and maintenance) is emerging as a very important 
pillar of the clean energy ecosystem.
Delivering this performance requires 
more than maintenance; it demands 
expertise, technology and disciplined 
execution. As India's only listed pure-play 
renewable operations and maintenance 
company, we work behind the scenes 
to keep renewable assets performing at 
their best. Managing an O&M portfolio 
exceeding 13 GWp across wind and 
solar assets (As on Mar-26), we combine 
engineering expertise, digital monitoring, 
predictive maintenance and data-
led insights to maximise equipment 
availability, improve generation 
efficiency and enhance the productivity 
of renewable infrastructure.
Our role is further amplified by the 
integrated capabilities of the INOXGFL 
Group. With a presence spanning wind 
turbine manufacturing, EPC, renewable 
power generation, solar manufacturing 
and O&M, the Group creates a connected renewable ecosystem 
where projects seamlessly transition 
from development and commissioning 
to long-term asset management. This 
integration enables us to participate 
across the renewable value chain 
while providing customers with the 
confidence of a partner backed by 
deep technical expertise and proven 
execution capabilities.
As India accelerates its transition 
towards a cleaner energy future, we 
remain focused on enabling renewable 
infrastructure to deliver its full potential. 
By combining operational excellence 
with technology-led asset management 
and a growing national footprint, 
we are helping transform installed 
renewable capacity into dependable, 
everyday power—supporting industries, 
communities and the nation's aspiration 
for a cleaner, more energy-secure future.Contents

About INOXGFL Group
The Power Behind 
Our Progress
INOXGFL Group is a multi-billion-dollar Indian conglomerate with a legacy spanning 
more than nine decades and three listed entities. The Group has established a 
diversified presence across chemicals and renewables, with businesses spanning 
fluoropolymers, fluorochemicals, battery chemicals, wind turbines, EPC, renewable 
O&M, solar cells and modules and renewable power generation.

About INOX Green
Performance that Powers 
a Greener Bharat
We are one of India’s leading renewable O&M services companies, delivering 
integrated asset management solutions across wind, solar and hybrid renewable 
energy projects. With one of the country’s largest renewable O&M portfolios, we 
play a critical role in maximising asset performance, improving plant availability and 
enabling reliable clean energy generation at scale.
As part of the INOXGFL 
Group, we benefit from 
an ecosystem that spans 
renewable manufacturing, 
EPC, power generation 
and asset management. 
This integrated model 
creates a natural pipeline of 
opportunities, enabling us to 
support renewable assets 
from commissioning through 
their operating life.
Our business is built on 
enduring partnerships 
with renewable energy 
developers and asset 
owners, anchored by 
multi-year service contracts 
that provide operational 
continuity for customers and 
predictable revenue visibility 
for our business.
Through predictive 
maintenance, 24x7 centralised 
monitoring and data-driven 
insights, we enhance 
machine availability, improve 
operational efficiency and 
enhance energy generation 
across the assets under our 
care. As India’s renewable 
energy sector gathers 
momentum, we are scaling 
alongside it—expanding our 
capabilities, broadening our 
portfolio and reinforcing 
our role as a trusted 
partner in safeguarding the 
performance of the nation’s 
clean energy infrastructure.

Message from the CEO
Steering the Way 
Forward
Delivering with Discipline
Our renewable O&M portfolio expanded 
to over 13 GWp during the year, 
comprising approximately 10.3 GW of 
wind assets, with the balance comprising 
solar assets. This growth was driven by 
strategic acquisitions and continued 
business expansion, strengthening our 
ability to serve customers across a 
diversified renewable asset base.
Operational excellence remains the 
foundation of our business. During 
FY2025-26, we maintained an 
average machine availability of 96.5%, 
reflecting the strength of our predictive 
maintenance practices, centralised 
monitoring capabilities and data-driven 
operating processes. These capabilities 
help minimise downtime, improve asset 
reliability and enable customers to 
maximise energy generation from their 
renewable assets.
While wind O&M continues to be the 
cornerstone of our business, we have 
steadily expanded our presence in the 
solar segment, enabling us to support 
customers across multiple renewable 
technologies. Our growing geographical 
footprint and diversified customer base 
reflect the confidence that customers 
place in our technical expertise, service 
quality and long-t erm commitment.
Building a More Agile 
Enterprise
During the year, we also completed an 
important strategic milestone with the 
demerger of the evacuation infrastructure 
business, transforming Inox Green into 
a focused, asset-light renewable O&M 
platform. This sharpened business model 
allows us to concentrate on our core 
strengths while reinforcing the recurring 
and annuity-led nature o f our revenues.
The resilience of this model was 
reflected in our financial performance. 
We continued to deliver healthy growth in income and profitability, supported 
by disciplined execution, operating 
leverage and the continued expansion 
of our operating portfolio. Long-term 
service contracts provide strong revenue 
visibility and stable cash flows, enabling 
us to invest in technology, people 
and future growth while maintaining 
financial discipline.
Creating New Growth 
Avenues
Our strategy balances organic growth 
with carefully evaluated inorganic 
opportunities. As part of the integrated 
INOXGFL renewable ecosystem, we 
benefit from a visible pipeline of long-term 
O&M opportunities as renewable assets 
developed by Group companies transition 
into the operational phase. This provides 
a strong foundation for organic growth 
while allowing us to participate across the 
renewable asset lifecycle.
Alongside this, we continue to pursue 
carefully evaluated acquisitions and 
third-party O&M mandates to expand our 
portfolio. During the year, our strategic 
acquisitions accelerated operating scale 
and strengthened our long-term growth 
platform. We also broadened our service 
offerings through specialised solutions 
such as wind turbine overhauls and life-
extension services, enabling customers to 
improve asset performance and maximise 
the productive life of their  installations.
By leveraging digital tools, predictive 
analytics and insights from our growing 
portfolio, we continue to strengthen 
maintenance planning, improve service 
responsiveness and drive greater 
operational efficiency across our network.
People, Purpose and 
Progress
As we grow, we remain equally 
committed to responsible business 
practices. We continue to uphold high standards of safety, governance and 
environmental stewardship across 
our operations while investing in the 
capabilities that will shape the future of 
the renewable energy sector. Our flagship 
Vayuveer programme is developing a 
skilled talent pipeline by equipping young 
professionals with industry-relevant 
capabilities, reinforcing our belief that 
long-term business success is built on 
strong people and stronger communities.
Building on Strong 
Foundations
Looking ahead, India’s renewable 
energy ambitions present a compelling 
opportunity for specialised O&M service 
providers. With an expanded operating 
portfolio, a focused asset-light business 
model, strong revenue visibility and 
multiple avenues for growth supported 
by both the INOXGFL ecosystem and 
strategic acquisitions, we are well 
positioned for the next phase of our 
journey. We will continue to strengthen 
our operational capabilities, deepen 
customer relationships, broaden our 
service offerings and pursue disciplined 
growth while remaining focused on 
creating sustainable long-term value.
I would like to express my sincere 
gratitude to our shareholders for their 
continued trust, our customers for their 
enduring partnership, our employees for 
their dedication and commitment and 
all our stakeholders for their unwavering 
support. Together, we remain committed 
to delivering operational excellence, 
advancing India’s renewable energy 
transition and creating lasting value 
while staying true to our purpose of 
‘Empowering a Greener Bharat’.
Warm regards,
S. K. Mathusudhana

The Formula for 
Enduring Success

is designed around

and disciplined capital

Operating Landscape
Delivering on Our Promise 
of a Cleaner Tomorrow
Every renewable asset commissioned today creates a decades-long requirement 
for efficient operations and maintenance. As India’s renewable energy capacity 
accelerates, the demand for specialised O&M services is expanding in parallel, 
making asset reliability, operational efficiency and performance optimisation 
increasingly critical for developers and asset owners.
Rising electricity demand, ambitious renewable capacity additions, growing adoption of hybrid projects and a supportive policy 
framework are reshaping the sector. Against this backdrop, organised O&M providers with technical expertise, digital capabilities and 
the ability to manage large, geographically dispersed portfolios are emerging as indispensable partners in India’s clean energy transition.

Key Enablers Supporting the Wind O&M Opportunity
Sustained demand for wind
Wind’s strategic role in the energy 
mixImmense capacity addition potential Favourable policy environment
 National Electricity Policy 2026 targets 
per capita electricity consumption of 
2,000 kWh by 2030 and over 4,000 
kWh by 2047, signalling sustained 
growth in India’s electricity demand.
 India targets 500 GW of non-fossil fuel 
capacity by 2030, creating a multi-
year capacity addition opportunity 
for renewables.
 Demand from commercial and 
industrial users, including data centers 
is expected to support renewable 
power procurement, aided by green 
open acce ss regulations.
 Wind generation complements solar 
output and supports hybrid / FDRE 
project structures.
 Nearly 45% of wind generation occurs 
during peak demand hours, enhancing 
grid reliability and supporting 
energy security.
 Hybrid, RTC and FDRE projects 
improve the relevance of wind by 
supporting better grid utilisation, 
more stable generation and improved 
project economics. India has 29.28 GW of wind 
projects under construction as 
on 31 March 2026.
 Another 19.00 GW of hybrid projects 
under construction adds to the future 
O&M opportunity.
 The offshore wind VGF scheme, with 
an outlay of H7,453 crore for 1 GW 
of offshore wind projects and port 
upgrades, further supports long-term 
sect or development. MNRE has prescribed an annual 
bidding trajectory of 50 GW renewable 
capacity until FY2028, with at 
least 10 GW per annum reserved 
for wind projects.
 Green Energy Open Access Rules 
allow consumers to procure green 
energy for part or all of their electricity 
consumption, supporting C&I demand.
 ALMM-Wind and ALMM-WTC 
frameworks support approved 
wind models, manufacturers and 
components, strengthening the 
domestic wind ecosystem.

Our Growth Strategy
Scaling New 
Possibilities
India’s accelerating renewable energy build-out is creating an expanding and 
enduring opportunity for specialised O&M services. Our strategy is to scale 
alongside this opportunity by broadening our renewable O&M portfolio, deepening 
customer relationships and extending our presence across both wind and solar 
assets. Driven by recurring service contracts, the INOXGFL ecosystem, disciplined 
capital allocation and technology-enabled execution, we are building a business 
defined by scale, operational excellence and resilient earnings.

contractor workforces, operating in

and regulatory compliance.
Our Maintenance Service
Maintenance services are a crucial 
component of renewable energy farm 
operations and represent a significant 
portion of the overall operational costs. 
The maintenance of Wind Turbine 
Generators (WTGs) and solar energy 
projects is typically categorized into 
predictive and reacti ve maintenance.
Reactive maintenance involves repairing 
components only after a failure has 
occurred, often resulting in prolonged 
downtimes and reduced energy 
generation. In contrast, predictive 
maintenance focuses on identifying 
potential failures in advance, enabling 
timely intervention to minimize disruptions 
and maximize turbine availability.
At Inox Green Energy Services Limited, 
we prioritize predictive maintenance by 
GRI 2. D. 2.1: - Organis ational detailsconducting scheduled inspections and routine servicing, with intensified efforts during 
peak wind seasons. We also leverage advanced technologies such as WT SCADA 
systems to continuously monitor the condition of WTGs, solar modules and associated 
infrastructure. This proactive approach facilitates early detection of anomalies and 
ensures prompt resolution, thereby enhancing the reliability and efficiency of our 
renewable energy assets.

GRI 3 D.3.3: - Management of material topicsMateriality Assessment: Our Approach
Institutionalizing Our Materiality Assessment
In Financial Year 2022–23, Inox Green Energy Services Limited conducted a comprehensive Materiality Assessment to systematically 
identify, evaluate, and prioritize the Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) topics most critical to our business resilience and 
stakeholder interests. This assessment serves as a cornerstone of our sustainability strategy, ensuring our ESG roadmap remains highly 
targeted, actionable, and aligned with global best practices.
Our materiality determination follows a structured, five-stage methodology:
Stakeholder Engagement 
We actively consult a diverse cross-
section of stakeholders—including 
investors, employees, customers, 
supply chain partners, and community 
representatives—to establish a balanced, 
multi-dimensional view of emerging ESG 
priorities and expectations.
Leadership Validation
The prioritized material topics undergo 
formal review and validation by executive 
management and the Board of Directors, 
ensuring alignment with enterprise 
risk management and long-term 
corporate vision.Strategic Integration
Validated material topics are integrated directly into our corporate ESG roadmap, 
shaping operational key performance indicators (KPIs), risk mitigation programs, and 
external reporting disclosures.
By institutionalizing this structured assessment, Inox Green Energy Services Limited 
ensures that its sustainability agenda is purpose-driven, stakeholder-informed, and 
strategically anchored to deliver lasting value and total operational transparency.Issue Identification
Synthesizing stakeholder input alongside 
global reporting frameworks, peer 
benchmarks, and internal strategic 
goals, we curate a broad repository of 
material issues relevant to our wind O&M 
operations and long-term value creation.Impact Prioritization
Each topic is scored across two 
fundamental dimensions: its overall 
importance to our stakeholder ecosystem 
and its potential financial or operational 
impact on our business. This matrix allows 
leadership to allocate resources where 
impact is highest.

At Inox Green Energy Services Limited, 
we are committed to maintaining 
the highest standards of corporate 
governance, founded on the principles 
of integrity, transparency, accountability, 
and ethical business conduct. As a part 
of the INOXGFL Group, we continue 
to uphold the Group's governance 
philosophy and values while ensuring 
compliance with all applicable statutory 
and regulatory requirements and aligning 
our practices with globally recognized 
governance standards.
Our governance framework is designed 
to support sustainable value creation by 
promoting responsible decision-making, 
effective risk management, and robust 
internal controls. The Board of Directors 
plays a pivotal role in defining the 
Company's strategic direction, overseeing 
operational and financial performance, 
safeguarding stakeholder interests, and 
ensuring long-term business resilience.
As on March 31, 2026, the Company's 
Board comprised six Directors, 
representing an appropriate mix 
of Executive, Non-Executive, and 
Independent Directors. The Board 
includes two Executive Directors, four Non-Executive Directors, of which 
three are Independent Directors, 
including one Woman Independent 
Director. This balanced composition 
enables objective oversight, independent 
judgment, and diversity of thought, 
thereby strengthening the overall 
governance framework.
The appointment of Directors is 
undertaken through a structured 
and transparent process led by the 
Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee (NRC). The Committee 
evaluates potential candidates based 
on their professional expertise, industry 
knowledge, leadership capabilities, 
governance experience, integrity, 
diversity, and ability to contribute to the 
Company's long-term strategic objectives. 
The Company remains committed 
to fostering an inclusive and diverse 
Board that reflects a broad spectrum of 
perspectives and competencies.
The Board is supported by its 
Committees, which facilitate focused 
oversight across critical governance 
areas, including audit, risk management, 
stakeholder relationship management, 
and nomination and remuneration matters. These Committees operate 
under clearly defined terms of reference 
and assist the Board in discharging its 
responsibilities effectively.
The Company has also designated 
a Chief Executive Officer (CEO), 
Chief Financial Officer (CFO), and 
Company Secretary (CS) as its Key 
Managerial Personnel (KMP). Together, 
the KMP provide strategic leadership, 
oversee financial stewardship, ensure 
regulatory and statutory compliance, 
strengthen governance practices, and 
drive operational excellence across 
the organization.
During FY 2025-26, the Company 
continued to reinforce its governance 
practices through regular Board and 
Committee meetings, periodic review 
of strategic and operational risks, 
monitoring of compliance obligations, 
enhancement of internal control systems, 
and adherence to the Company's Code of 
Conduct and ethical business principles. 
These governance practices enable the 
Company to operate responsibly, manage 
emerging risks effectively, and create 
sustainable value for all stakeholders.Our Leadership Team

Corporate Social Responsibility Committee
Business Responsibility & Sustainability CommitteeIn accordance with the provisions of Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, read with the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility 
Policy) Rules, 2014, the Company has constituted a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Committee of the Board to oversee the 
planning, implementation, monitoring, and review of its CSR initiatives.
The CSR Committee is responsible for formulating and recommending the Company’s CSR Policy, identifying and approving CSR 
projects and programmes, monitoring the implementation and utilization of CSR funds, and ensuring compliance with applicable 
statutory requirements. The Committee periodically reviews the progress and impact of CSR initiatives and provides strategic guidance 
to ensure that the Company’s CSR activities contribute meaningfully to sustainable community development and create positive social 
and environmental impact in alignment with the Company’s values and long-term sustainability objectives.
Recognizing the increasing importance of sustainability in creating long-term stakeholder value, the Company has constituted a 
Business Responsibility and Sustainability (BRS) Committee of the Board. The Committee provides strategic oversight on the Company’s 
environmental, social, and governance (ESG) initiatives and supports the integration of sustainability principles into business strategy, 
risk management, and decision-making processes.
The Committee is responsible for overseeing the implementation of the Company’s Business Responsibility and Sustainability 
framework, monitoring progress against key ESG objectives, reviewing sustainability-related risks and opportunities, guiding ESG 
disclosures, and promoting responsible business practices in alignment with the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct 
(NGRBCs) and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 20 15, as amended.

into the effectiveness of our family-friendly policies and initiatives. It also underscores our commitment to supporting both

dedication to building a diverse, supportive, and sustainable workplace culture.

Our waste management strategy rests on three opera tional pillars:
Over the past three financial years, we have systematically deployed targeted conservation measures across our administrative facilities 
and operational sites. These initiatives include installing high-efficiency water fixtures, conducting routine preventive maintenance to 
eliminate line leakages, and establishing continuous consumption monitoring. Driven by these proactive controls, our total annual water 
footprint has decreased significantly over successive rep orting periods:We have instituted a comprehensive Waste Lifecycle Management System that governs every stage of waste generation across 
our wind farms and administrative offices—from classification and source segregation to safe handling, temporary storage, and 
environmentally sound disposal. To ensure strict adherence to statutory norms, all regulated waste streams are handled exclusively 
through verified, state-authorized waste management partners.

Management Discussion and Analysis
Economic Overview
Global Economic Overview1 
The global economy in CY 2025 operated within a complex 
macroeconomic environment characterised by geopolitical tensions, 
shifting trade dynamics and structural supply chain realignments. 
Despite these headwinds, the global output expanded by 3.5%, 
supported by policy interventions and sustained momentum in 
technology-related investment. Global inflation moderated to 4.1% in 
CY 2025 compared with previous years, reflecting country-specific 
influences including import tariff adjustments, subdued food prices 
and fiscal measures. However, price levels remained exposed to 
volatility, particularly in energy markets. 
Growth in advanced economies moderated to 1.9% in CY 2025, 
driven by elevated interest rates. Emerging market and developing 
economies achieved higher growth at 4.5%, supported by 
technology-enabled trade flo ws across Asia.
In the beginning of 2026, heightened geopolitical tensions, 
particularly in West Asia, had a material impact on global economic 
conditions. These developments disrupted global activity, driven 
by rising commodity prices, firmer inflation expectations and 
tighter financial conditions, which collectively tested the resilience 
of markets worldwide.
Outlook2 
Global growth is projected to moderate to 3.0% in CY 2026, 
before a modest recovery to 3.4% in CY 2027, weighed down by 
geopolitical disruptions, elevated commodity prices and persistent 
structural constraints. Global headline inflation is projected at 4.7% 
in CY 2026, driven by rising energy a nd food prices.
While active hostilities in the Middle East have eased, the region 
continues to present geopolitical risks to the global outlook, 
with potential implications for commodity markets, inflation 
expectations and financial stability. Although immediate concerns 
over disruptions to major energy infrastructure and critical trade 
routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, have moderated, any 
renewed escalation could materially affect global hydrocarbon 
supply and intensify energy market pressures. Growth prospects 
remain uneven, leaving emerging and developing economies that 
are net commodity importers particularly vulnerable to inflationary 
pressures, currency volatility and e xternal shocks.
Over the medium term, structural impediments and increasing 
geo-economic fragmentation are expected to constrain global 
growth. However, productivity gains arising from technological 
advancements could partially offset these challenges, supported by 
effective policy frameworks and greater international coordination.Global Real GDP Growth Projections (%)

Indian Economic Overview3
During FY 2025-26, India outperformed most major economies due 
to steady public investment, solid macroeconomic fundamentals 
and resilient domestic demand. Real GDP grew at 7.7%, with private 
consumption and investment serving as the principal drivers of 
economic expansion. Consumer price inflation moderated to 3.4%, 
allowing the Reserve Bank of India to reduce the policy repo rate 
by a cumulative 100 basis points.
Aggregate demand remained resilient, anchored by Private 
Final Consumption Expenditure, which continued to serve as the 
primary pillar of domestic demand. The Government sustained 
its emphasis on infrastructure-led development, allocating capital 
expenditure of H11.21 lakh crore in the Union Budget 2025-26, while 
advancing its clean energy priorities.4 India also made significant 
progress in renewable energy deployment, reinforcing the 
credibility of its updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 
commitments. Continued expansion of solar and wind capacity, 
supported by enabling policy measures and increased investment 
in clean energy infrastructure, has strengthened the country's 
transition towards a low-carbon economy.

growth is projected at 6.6% in FY 2026-27, driven primarily by 
private consumption and capital formation. The Reserve Bank of 
India has projected CPI inflation at 5.1% for FY2026-27, reflecting 
risks arising from geopolitical uncertainties and weather-
related factors.
In alignment with the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, India has outlined 
an ambitious renewable energy roadmap and achieved a major 
milestone in its energy transition journey by attaining 50% non-
fossil fuel-based power generation capacity in 2025, five years 
ahead of its 2030 target. 
Further momentum is expected from Phase III of the EU-India Clean 
Energy and Climate Partnership (CECP) as well as the free trade 
agreement with the United Kingdom, which aim to promote industry-
led collaboration in solar, wind and green hydrogen technologies. 
These initiatives are projected to facilitate greater trade, investment 
and technology exchange. Together, these developments are 
likely to support resilient supply chains, encourage innovation and 
accelerate the deployment of clean ener gy solutions.6

Industry Overview
Global Renewable Energy Sector
In 2025, global renewable power capacity reached 5,149 GW, 
following the addition of 692 GW during the year. This marked 
a 15.5% increase and the fastest annual growth on record. The 
sector is undergoing structural change, underpinned by declining 
levelized costs of energy and policy frameworks promoting net 
zero emissions, driving investments in wind, solar PV and battery 
storage. Global renewable electricity generation rose by 9% in 
2025, marking a significant shift in the global power generation 
landscape.13 The transition towards renewable energy is expected 
to gain further momentum, with renewable sources projected to 
account for nearly 43% of global electricity generation by 2030, 
driven by sustained expansion in solar and wind capacity.14 
Renewable energy capacity additions are estimated to remain 
robust, with approximately 4,600 GW of new capacity additions 
anticipated between 2025 and 2030, effectively doubling the 
installed base. Rising electricity demand, driven by electrification, 
digitalisation and industrial decarbonisation, is expected to be 
increasingly met by renewable sources, reinforcing their role as a 
cornerstone of the future energy system.15 Global Wind O&M Market
The global wind sector added approximately 165 GW in 2025 
(representing a 40% increase), taking cumulative installations 
to around 1,299 GW. Growth was supported by rising electricity 
demand, energy security considerations and continued policy 
support across major markets. Wind power maintained its position 
as a crucial component of the global energy mix, with capacity 
additions recorded in both developed and emerging economies. 
Annual new wind installations are projected to reach a record 178 
GW in 2026. Supported by existing policy frameworks and the 
global response to the Middle East crisis, cumulative new wind 
capacity additions are expected to total 969 GW during 2026–
2030, averaging approximately 194 GW annually16, maintaining a 
robust CAGR of 5.2% over the 2026–2030 period.
The growing installed base has significantly expanded the 
requirement for specialised operations and maintenance (O&M) 
services to maximise asset availability, optimise performance 
and extend turbine life. Demand for O&M services is being 
further driven by the ageing turbine fleet, increasingly challenging 
operating environments and the deployment of larger, more 
complex turbine platforms.

Indian Renewable Energy Sector
FY2025-26 marked a significant milestone in India's clean energy 
transition, with non-fossil fuel sources accounting for more than 
50% of the country's installed power generation capacity. Total 
non-fossil capacity reached approximately 283.46 GW, including 
274.68 GW of renewable energ y capacity.19  
India’s renewable energy expansion is expected to accelerate 
further as the country advances towards its target of 500 GW of 
non-fossil capacity by 2030.20 Over the longer term, total installed 
power generation capacity is projected to exceed 1,121 GW by FY 
2035-36, with non-fossil sources likely to account for a substantial 
share. Solar capacity is projected to reach 509 GW and wind 
capacity is expected to increase to 155 GW. 
Electricity demand is projected to rise to approximately 3,365

expansion and electrification.21 This creates a long-duration 
opportunity for renewable energy O&M serv ices providers.
Government Policy Support22 
ISTS Charge Waiver: The Government of India has supported 
renewable energy development through the waiver of Inter-State 
Transmission System (ISTS) charges for solar and wind power 
projects. Projects commissioned up to 30 June 2025 are eligible 
for a full waiver, while projects commissioned thereafter will 
receive progressively lower benefits until June 2028. By lowering 
power transmission costs, the policy has improved project 
viability, encouraged investment and facilitated wider deployment 
of clean energy across the country. CERC (Sharing of Inter-
State Transmission Charges and Losses) (Fourth Amendment) 
Regulations, 2025 issued on 26.06.2025 to provide ISTS waiver 
trajectory for RE and BESS projects, including provision of 
extension of waiver in case of delay on account of Force Majeure 
event including non-availability of transmission system or for 
reasons not attributable to the Renewable Energy Generator.
GST rate cut: The GST rate on wind turbines, solar modules and 
other renewable energy devices was reduced from 12% to 5%, 
w.e.f. September 22, 2025. The measure is expected to reduce 
project costs, improve affordability and support faster renewable 
energy deployment.
Standard Bidding Guidelines: The Government has introduced 
standard bidding guidelines for tariff-based competitive 
procurement of power from grid-connected solar, wind, wind-
solar hybrid and firm and dispatchable renewable energy projects. 
The framework has enhanced transparency and consistency in 
the bidding process, encouraged greater competition among 
developers and contributed to improved investor confidence.Wind ALMM: To promote domestic manufacturing, the MNRE 
has amended the procedure for inclusion/updating wind turbine 
models in the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers of 
Wind Turbines (ALMM-Wind). This was issued on 31st July 2025 
and the related Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs) were 
issued on 29.10.2025.
Basic Customs Duty Exemption: BCD exemption extended to 
capital goods for lithium-ion cell manufacturing for Battery Energy 
Storage Systems (effective 2 February 2026 to 31 March 2028). 
This will reduce the reliance on imported battery packs, primarily 
from China, strengthening India's Atmanirbhar Bharat goals in 
the energy sector.
REEIMS Portal: Renewable Energy Equipment Import Monitoring 
System (REEIMS) portal, launched in October 2025 enabled real-
time tracking of import patterns of critical renewable energy 
equipment, ensuring greater supply chain transparency, regulatory 
compliance, and prevention of misuse of impor ted components.
RCO Framework: On the recommendation of MNRE, MoP has 
revised the Renewable Consumption Obligation) RCO compliance 
framework under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, superseding 
the earlier October 2023 notification. State-level RPO targets are 
subsumed within this unified RCO framework, eliminating dual 
obligations under the Electricity Act, 2003.
GNA Regulations: CERC (Connectivity and General Network 
Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) (Third 
Amendment) Regulations, 2025 introduced a non-solar hour 
connectivity framework. This will help in better utilization of the 
transmission network.
Virtual Power Purchase Agreements: Guidelines for Virtual 
Power Purchase Agreements (VPPA) issued by CERC. VPPA 
provides an additional instrument to enable the Designated 
Consumers to meet their RCO targets.
Contract for Difference: Pilot Scheme for Contract for Difference 
(CfD) for RE projects of 500 MW capacity issued by MNRE. The 
CfD mechanism, a globally proven framework, guarantees stable 
revenues to renewable energy developers while preserving 
competitive, market-based price discovery.
Geothermal Energy: The National Policy on Geothermal Energy 
was issued in September 2025, providing a comprehensive 
strategic framework to accelerate the exploration, development, and 
commercial utilization of geothermal resources across the country.
Human Resource Development: The Ministry has formally 
inaugurated the Jaiv-Urja Mitra programme under the Human 
Resource Development (HRD) framework. This strategic initiative 
is designed to bolster the renewable energy value chain by 
providing specialized technical training and capacity-building 
for key stakeholders, including biomass aggregators, feedstock 
depot operators, and Compressed Biogas (CB G) technicians.

Growth Drivers
Favourable Policy Framework
India's target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity 
by 2030 is supported by progressively increasing Renewable 
Purchase Obligations (RPOs), which are expected to reach 
43.33% by FY2030. Additional support is provided through Inter-
State Transmission System (ISTS) charge waivers and demand-
generation initiatives such as PM Surya Ghar and PM-KUSUM. 
These measures provide visibility for future renewable capacity 
additions and support sustained demand for O&M services.33 
Rapid Capacity Expansion Driving O&M Demand 
India added a record 55.3 GW of non-fossil capacity in FY2025-
26, increasing total non-fossil installed capacity to 283 GW and 
reinforcing its position as the world's third-largest renewable 
energy market. Solar capacity surpassed 150 GW, while wind capacity crossed 56 GW following its best-ever annual 
addition of 6.05 GW and in July 2025, renewables met 51.5% 
of the country's electricity demand for the first time. This scale 
of growth translates directly into a rapidly expanding base of 
assets requiring long-term, professional O&M services.34 
Evolution of Integrated Renewable Energy Systems
India's renewable energy landscape is evolving from standalone wind 
and solar projects towards more complex configurations, including 
wind-solar hybrid projects, Round-the-Clock (RTC) solutions and 
Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) projects. The 
National Electricity Plan (2026-35) projects a requirement of 509 
GW of solar capacity, 155 GW of wind capacity and 174 GW of energy 
storage capacity by FY2035-36. The increasing complexity of these 
integrated energy systems is expected to create opportunities for 
specialised multi-technology O&M providers.34

Managing Asset Complexity at Scale
As renewable portfolios expand, operators face increasing challenges related to technology diversity, process standardisation and 
fragmented data environments. Effective asset management requires integrated systems, standardised operating practices and 
robust performance monitoring frameworks.
Downtime and Reactive Maintenance
Limited visibility into asset health can result in reactive maintenance practices and unplanned outages. Such disruptions adversely affect 
plant availability, operational efficiency and asset performance, highlighting the importance of predictive maintenanc e capabilities.

technical capabilities, maintaining training standards and ensuring clear operational accountability are essential for supporting long-

Company Overview
Inox Green Energy Services Limited (Inox Green) is a pure play renewable energy Operations and Maintenance (O&M) services company. 
Over the course of FY26, the Company significantly expanded its operating scale and evolved into one of India's leading integrated 
renewable energy O&M service providers.
As a subsidiary of Inox Wind Limited and an integral part of the diversified INOXGFL Group, Inox Green is uniquely positioned to support 
India's accelerating clean energy transition. Its core focus is the provision of long-term O&M services for Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs), 
solar projects, hybrid assets and battery energy storage systems (BESS), along with the associated common infrastructure required for 
efficient po wer evacuation.
90

=== page 53 ===
 During FY2025-26, the Company advanced its inorganic growth agenda by emerging as the successful bidder for Wind World 
(India) Limited’s ~4.5 GW wind O&M portfolio through an NCLT-approved resolution process. Subsequent to the year-end, 
the Company received approval from the Hon’ble NCLT, Ahmedabad, with transaction completion expected in Q2 FY27. The 
acquisition is expected to strengthen the Company’s scale, customer access and operational depth across key wind-rich states.
 Following the expansion of its solar O&M business and the announced acquisition of Wind World India’s O&M business during 
FY26, the Company's total renewable O&M portfolio increased to over 13 GWp, marking a significant step-up in scale and 
reinforcing its position as a leading O&M service prov ider in India. 
 The Company successfully expanded its solar O&M portfolio from a negligible base at the beginning of FY26 to approx. 3 GWp 
within the year, driven by multiple contract wins, including a significant project at Bhadla Solar Park. This marks the Company's 
strategic diversification beyond wind into solar, hybrid and BESS O&M services.
 During FY26, the Company delivered strong financial performance, with revenue of H 426 crs, EBITDA of H 210 crs, reported PAT 
of H 103 crs and Cash PAT of Rs. 158 crs, reflecting benefits of operating leverage and its asset-light business model.
 The Company further enhanced its technology backbone through SCADA-based real-time monitoring and analysis of assets, 
with SAP HANA upgradation underway.
 The demerger of the power evacuation business from Inox Green into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited has been completed as 
on August 1, 2026. This has sharpened the Company’s asset-light structure and strengthened its focus as a dedicated renewable 
O&M services provider.

 O&M opportunities linked to Inox Wind Limited’s order book of ~4.4 GW as on July 2026, where O&M services are typically 
bundled with turbine supply contracts.
 Expansion of the wind, solar, hybrid and BESS O&M portfolio supported by the anticipated growth of Inox Clean Energy, the 
Group’s Independent Power Producer (IPP) and solar module and cell manufacturing platform and the execution of future solar/
hybrid/RTC/FDRE projects. Inox Clean is targeting 10 GW of installed renewable energy capacity by FY28 and 11 GW of module 
manufacturing capacity by FY28, thereby creating a growing captiv e O&M pipeline.
Inorganic Growth Opportunities
 The Indian wind O&M market presents an estimated opportunity of approximately 10 GW from assets owned by inactive, 
distressed or under-serv iced operators.
 Further, there are a few renewable O&M players willing to divest stakes for str ategic reasons.
 The Company is well positioned to capitalise on these opportunities through its operational expertise, technical capabilities and 
execution track record.
 The successful acquisition of Wind World India's O&M business demonstrates the Company's ability to identify, evaluate and 
integrate large-scale strategic opportunities.Key Developments During FY26

Human Resources
INOX Green recognizes that its employees are essential to its 
continuous growth and success. As a result, the company's HR strategy 
emphasizes excellence in attracting and retaining top industry talent. 
To provide continuous skill development, the company hosts training 
programs, workshops, and certification courses. These initiatives 
keep employees updated on the newest industry developments and 
practices, allowing them to effectively support the c ompany's goals.
The company supports open communication and teamwork 
among all employee levels, prompting staff to work together 
toward common goals. Additionally, the company aims to build 
a positive and engaging workplace, which allows employees to 
make a significa nt difference. 
The company follows a Code of Conduct for trading to comply

Outlook
The Company has set a target of expanding its renewable energy 
O&M portfolio to approximately 20 GW over the next two years, 
supported by a balanced combination of organic growth initiatives 
and strategic inorganic opportunities.
A key milestone in this growth journey is the Wind World India 
Limited O&M acquisition, for which the Company has received 
approval from the Hon’ble NCLT, Ahmedabad. The transaction is 
expected to add ~4.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets, with 
completion expected in Q2 FY27.

Risk Management
The Company operates in a dynamic and rapidly evolving renewable energy sector. Effective risk management remains integral to 
preserving operational resilience, supporting sustainable growth and safeguarding stakeholder value. Key risks and mitigation measures 
are outlined below:
Risk Potential Impact Mitigation Strategy
Competitive 
PressuresIntensifying competition within the 
renewable energy services sector may 
exert pressure on market share, pricing 
and profitability.The Company focuses on delivering differentiated value through 
predictive maintenance, operational excellence, technology-
enabled service delivery and long-term customer relationships. 
These capabilities support asset performance and enhance 
customer retention.
Regulatory 
ChallengesChanges in government policies, incentive 
structures, tariff mechanisms or renewable 
energy regulations may influence sector 
growth and investment activity.The Company actively monitors policy developments and 
regulatory changes. Regular engagement with industry 
stakeholders and proactive business planning support timely 
responses to evolving regulatory requirements.
Technological 
RiskRapid technological advancements may 
alter operating requirements and create 
competitive advantages for market 
participants with superior capabilities.The Company continues to invest in digital infrastructure, including 
24x7 centralised asset monitoring, advanced SCADA analytics, mobile-
enabled O&M management platforms and SAP HANA implementation 
to enhance operational efficiency and technological readiness.
Geographic 
Concentration RiskDependence on wind-rich regions may 
limit growth opportunities and expose 
operations to regional market dynamics.The Company maintains a diversified operational presence across 
multiple renewable energy corridors and is expanding its footprint 
through solar, hybrid, RTC/FDRE and BESS O&M services, reducing 
reliance on any single geography or technology segment.
Workforce 
Availability RiskShortages of skilled technical personnel 
and employee attrition may affect service 
quality, operational efficiency and business 
scalability.The Company invests in structured training, capability-building 
programmes and employee development initiatives to enhance 
workforce competencies, improve retention and support future 
growth requirements.
Third-party 
Transaction RiskBusiness relationships with vendors, 
contractors and other external stakeholders 
may expose the Company to operational, 
commercial and compliance-related risks.IGESL follows established governance processes, due diligence 
procedures and contractual safeguards to promote transparency, 
mitigate conflicts of interest and support fair and ethical business 
practices.
Contract 
related RiskDelays in project execution, contract 
modifications, non-renewals or 
cancellations may affect revenue visibility 
and growth prospects.IGESL enters into comprehensive contractual arrangements that 
clearly define responsibilities, service scope and risk allocation. 
Long-standing customer relationships and proactive engagement 
support effective issue resolution and contract continuity.

Internal Control Systems
The Company has established a robust internal control framework 
commensurate with the scale, complexity and growth trajectory 
of its operations. The framework is designed to ensure accuracy 
and completeness of financial reporting, safeguard the Company 
assets, ensure regulatory compliance and support the governance 
standards expected of a listed public company.
The key elements of the internal control architecture include a 
well-defined organisational structure with clear authority matrices, 
comprehensive policies and standard operating procedures 
and technology-enabled controls through ERP systems, CRM 
integration and a Shared Services Centre. The Company 
has completed the transition to SAP HANA, which became 
operationally effective during FY26, significantly strengthening 
enterprise resource planning, financial visibility and operational 
data management across its expanding portfolio.
A centralised Revenue Assurance function ensures accuracy in 
billing, contract compliance and collections monitoring, which is 
particularly important given the Company's annuity-driven revenue 
model across a large number of O&M contracts. Frequent internal 
audits are conducted and the Audit Committee of the Board 
periodically reviews the adequacy and operating effectiveness of 
these controls. The internal audit function reports independently 
to the Audit Committee, ensuring its objectivity and authority.The Code of Conduct framework and Whistleblower Policy are 
overseen by a dedicated committee to maintain ethical standards 
across the organisation. The Vigil Mechanism provides employees 
and directors a safe, protected channel to report concerns 
directly to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee, without fear 
of victimisation.

Item Nos. 6 and 7
The Company is one of India's leading renewable operations and 
maintenance service providers, engaged in providing operations 
and maintenance services for wind and solar energy projects and 
other allied renewable energy infrastructure assets.
The Company forms part of the INOXGFL Group's integrated 
renewable energy platform, under which various Group entities 
are engaged in complementary businesses across the renewable 
energy value chain, including manufacture and supply of 
wind turbine generators and related equipment, engineering, 
procurement and construction services, renewable energy 
project development and other allied activities.
Given the integrated nature of the Group's renewable energy 
business, the Company and, wherever applicable, its subsidiaries, 
regularly undertake transactions with various Group entities 
to meet customer requirements, facilitate integrated business 
arrangements, support project execution and operational 
requirements, optimise working capital and funding requirements 
and efficiently conduct their business operations. These 
transactions include, inter alia, purchase and sale of goods and 
services, operational and project support arrangements, working 
capital, funding and other financial arrangements required for the 
efficient conduct of business.The proposed related party transactions are undertaken as part of 
the Company's integrated business model and are critical for the 
efficient conduct and growth of its business. These transactions, 
inter alia, provide the following benefits:
	 Operational efficiency through integration of services, 
procurement and execution across Group entities;
	 Cost optimisation driven by economies of scale, shared 
infrastructure and procurement advantages;
	 Access to technical expertise, execution capabilities and 
specialised resources available within the Group;
	 Improved project execution timelines and operational 
reliability; and
	 Strategic alignment with the Company's long-term growth 
plans and expansion of its pr oject pipeline.
Having regard to the nature of the Company's business, these 
transactions are repetitive and continuous in nature and are 
undertaken from time to time depending upon business 
requirements, project execution schedules, commercial 
opportunities, operational exigencies and working capital and 
funding requirements. Accordingly, approval of the Members is 
being sought for enabling the Company and, wherever applicable, 
its subsidiaries to enter into such related party transactions during 
the approval period within the limits proposed in the resolutions. 
The proposed limits are enabling in nature and intended to provide 
adequate operational and financial flexibility. Actual transaction 
values may vary depending on business requirements and may 
be lower than the a pproved limits.
All related party transactions of the Company and its subsidiaries 
are undertaken in the ordinary course of business and on an 
arm's length basis in accordance with applicable laws and the 
Company's Policy on Related Party Transactions. The pricing and 
commercial terms are determined based on prevailing market 
prices, comparable third-party quotations, cost-plus arrangements 
or other generally accepted pricing methodologies, as may be 
applicable having regard to the nature of the transaction. 
All such transactions are subject to prior approval and periodic 
review by the Audit Committee in accordance with applicable 
laws and the Company's Policy on Related Party Transactions. 
The related party transactions proposed to be entered into by 
the subsidiaries, as set out in this Notice, are also subject to the 
approval of the Audit Committee and/ or the Board of Directors of 
the respective subsidiaries, where ver applicable.
Pursuant to Regulation 23 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 ("Listing Regulations"), 
material related party transactions and subsequent material 
modifications thereto require prior approval of the shareholders of 
the listed entity by way of an ordina ry resolution. 
Based on the Company's last audited consolidated financial 
statements for the Financial Year ended 31st March, 2026, the 
annual consolidated turnover of the Company is H 281 Crore.

Company falls within the first prescribed slab applicable to 
listed entities having an annual consolidated turnover of upto

warrant, including a premium of H 135/- per warrant, for

Six Hundred and Fifty Crore only), to both ‘Promoter’ 
and ‘Non-Promoter’ entities, with a right to the warrant 
holders to apply for and be allotted 1 (One) equity share 
of face value of H 10/- each, in one or more tranches,

the issue price.

 Owing to the non-exercise of conversion rights in respect

6. Scheme of Demerger
 The Scheme of Arrangement between Inox Green Energy 
Services Limited (“Demerged Company” or “the Company”) 
and Inox Renewable Solutions Limited (formerly known 
as Resco Global Wind Services Private Limited) (“IRSL” or 
“Resulting Company”) and their respective shareholders 
(the “Scheme”), providing for the demerger of the Power 
Evacuation Business of the Company into the Resulting 
Company, was approved by the Hon’ble National Company 
Law Tribunal, Ahmedabad Bench (“NCLT”) vide its order 
dated 13th March, 2026.
 The certified copy of the NCLT order was filed by both the 
companies with the Registrar of Companies on 4th May, 2026, 
and accordingly, the Scheme became effective from 4th May, 
2026, with the Appointed Date being 1st October, 2024.
 The swap ratio as approved under the Scheme was as follows:
	 122 equity shares of face value H 10/- each of IRSL to be 
issued for every 1,000 equity shares of face value H 10/- 
each held in the Company; and	 122 share warrants of IRSL, having an issue price of H 
205/- per warrant, to be issued for every 1,000 share 
warrants of the Company having an issue price of H 
145/- per warrant.
 The Company fixed 1st August, 2026 as the Record Date 
for the purpose of determining the equity shareholders 
of the Demerged Company who were entitled to receive 
equity shares of the Resulting Company in accordance with 
the Scheme. As no share warrants of the Company were 
outstanding as on the Record Date, the warrant entitlement 
prescribed under the Scheme was not applicable.
 The Resulting Company is yet to make the allotment 
of equity shares to the eligible shareholders of the 
Company in accordance with the swap ratio prescribed 
under the Scheme.

Conservation of Energy and Technology Absorption
A. Conservation of Energy
 (i) Steps taken or impact on conservation of energy
  As a leading wind operations and maintenance 
(O&M) service provider, the Company is committed 
to improving energy efficiency across its operations. 
The Company focuses on preventive maintenance of 
wind turbines, optimization of maintenance activities, 
increased use of digital monitoring and analytics, 
and efficient utilization of resources at its offices 
and project sites.
  These initiatives help improve the operational 
performance and reliability of wind assets, reduce 
unplanned downtime, optimize resource utilization, and 
support cost efficiency. The Company continues to 
adopt best practices and technology-driven solutions 
to enhance operational efficiency while promoting 
sustainable and responsible business operation
 (ii) Steps taken for utilizing alternate sources of energy
  The Company operates in the renewable energy sector 
by providing operations and maintenance (O&M) 
services for wind energy projects. While the Company 
did not commission any alternate source of energy for 
its own operations during the year, its core business 
supports the efficient operation and maintenance 
of wind energy assets, thereby contributing to the 
generation of clean and renewable energy.
  The Company remains committed to supporting the 
growth of renewable energy through reliable, efficient, 
and technology-driven O&M services.
 (iii) Capital investment on energy conservation equipment
  During the financial year under review, the Company did 
not make any material capital investment specifically 
for energy conservation equipment. However, it 
continues to invest in energy-efficient equipment, 
digital technologies, and process improvements, as 
and when required, to improve operational efficiency, 
optimize resource utilization, and support sustainable 
business operations.B. Technology Absorption
 (i) Efforts made towards technology absorption
  The Company continues to adopt modern technologies 
and digital solutions to improve the operation and 
maintenance of wind turbine generators. These include 
remote monitoring systems, predictive maintenance, 
condition monitoring, data analytics, and digital 
reporting tools to improve asset performance, reduce 
downtime, and enhance operational efficiency.
  The Company remains focused on leveraging 
technology to deliver reliable, cost-effective, and high-
quality O&M services to its customers.
 (ii) Benefits derived from technology absorption
  The Company's technology initiatives ha ve resulted in:
	 Improved operational efficiency and productivity.
	 Higher availability and reliability of wind 
turbine generators.
	 Reduced equipment downtime through 
predicti ve maintenance.
	 Better planning and execution of 
maintena nce activities.
	 Enhanced customer service and overall 
operational performance.
 (iii) Imported technology (Imported during the last 
three years reckoned from the beginning of the 
financial year)
  During the financial year under review, the Company did 
not import any technology. Accordingly, the disclosure 
relating to imported technology, including the year of 
import, the status of technology absorption, and areas 
where absorption has not taken place, is not applicable.
 (iv) Expenditure incurred on Research and Development
  The Company has not incurred any material expenditure 
on research and development during the financial year.

3. AUDIT COMMITTEE
(A) BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF TERMS OF REFERENCE
 The Role and the Terms of Reference of Audit Committee 
are in accordance with the requirements of Section 177 of 
the Companies Act, 2013 read with relevant Rules made 
thereunder and Regulation 18 of the Listing Regulations read 
with Part C of Schedule II of the Listing Regulations.
 The Audit Committee plays a critical role in ensuring integrity 
of financial reporting and effectiveness of internal control 
systems. Its key terms of ref erence include:
 (a) Oversight of the Company’s financial reporting process, 
examination of the financial statement and the auditors’ 
report thereon and the disclosure of its financial 
information to ensure that the financial statement is 
correct, sufficien t and credible;
 (b) Recommendation for appointment, re-appointment 
and replacement, remuneration and terms of 
appointment of auditors, including the internal auditor, 
cost auditor and statutory auditor, of the Company and 
the fixation of audit fee; 
 (c) Approval of payments to statutory auditors for any 
other services rendered by the statutory auditors 
of the Company;
 (d) Reviewing, with the management, the annual 
financial statements and auditor’s report thereon 
before submission to the Board for approval, with 
particula r reference to:
  (i) Matters required to be included in the Director’s 
Responsibility Statement to be included in the 
Board’s report in terms of section 134(3) of the 
Companies Act; 
  (ii) Changes, if any, in accounting policies and 
practices and reasons for the same;   (iii) Major accounting entries involving estimates 
based on the exercise of judgment by the 
management of the Company;
  (iv) Significant adjustments made in the financial 
statements arising out of a udit findings; 
  (v) Compliance with listing and other legal 
requirements relating to financial statements; 
  (vi) Disclosure of any related party tra nsactions; and 
  (vii)  Qualifications / modified opinion(s) in the 
draft audit report. 
 (e) Reviewing, with the management, the quarterly, 
half-yearly and annual financial statements before 
submission to the Board for approval; 
 (f) Reviewing, with the management, the statement of 
uses/application of funds raised through an issue 
(public issue, rights issue, preferential issue, etc.), the 
statement of funds utilised for purposes other than 
those stated in the offer document/prospectus/notice 
and the report submitted by the monitoring agency 
monitoring the utilisation of proceeds of a public or 
rights issue, and making appropriate recommendations 
to the Board to take up steps in this matter. This 
also includes monitoring the use/ application of the 
funds raised through the proposed initial public offer 
by the Company; 
 (g) Reviewing and monitoring the auditor’s independence 
and performance, and effectiveness of audit process; 
 (h) Formulating a policy on related party transactions, which 
shall include materiality of related party transactions; 
 (i) Approval or any subsequent modification of 
transactions of the Company with related parties

4. NOMINATION AND REMUNERATION COMMITTEE
(A) BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF TERMS OF REFERENCE 
 The Role and the Terms of Reference of Nomination 
and Remuneration Committee (“NR Committee”) are in 
accordance with the requirements of Section 178 of the 
Companies Act, 2013 read with relevant Rules made 
thereunder and Regulation 19 of the Listing Regulations read 
with Part D of Schedule II of the Listing Regulations.
 The NR Committee is entrusted with key responsibilities 
relating to Board composition, evaluation and remuneration, 
in line with applicable regulatory requirements. The brief 
terms of reference of the Committee are set out below:
 (a) Formulation of the criteria for determining qualifications, 
positive attributes and independence of a director 
and recommend to the Board a policy, relating to 
the remuneration of the directors, key managerial 
personnel and o ther employees;
  The Nomination and Remuneration Committee, while 
formulating the above policy, should ensure that
  (i) the level and composition of remuneration be 
reasonable and sufficient to attract, retain and 
motivate directors of the quality required to run 
our Company successfully; 
  (ii) relationship of remuneration to performance 
is clear and meets appropriate performance 
benchmarks; and 
  (iii) remuneration to directors, key managerial 
personnel and senior management involves 
a balance between fixed and incentive pay 
reflecting short- and long-term performance 
objectives appropriate to the working of the 
Company and its goals.
 (b) For every appointment of an independent director, the 
Nomination and Remuneration Committee shall evaluate 
the balance of skills, knowledge and experience on the 
Board and on the basis of such evaluation, prepare a 
description of the role and capabilities required of an 
independent director. The person recommended to 
the Board for appointment as an independent director 
shall have the capabilities identified in such description. 
For the purpose of identifying suitable candidates, 
the Committee may:
  (i) use the services of an external agencies, if required;
  (ii) consider candidates from a wide range of 
backgrounds, having due regard to diversity; and
  (iii) consider the time commitments of the candidates.
 (c) Formulation of criteria for evaluation of performance of 
independent directors and the Board;
 (d) Devising a policy on Board diversity; (e) Identifying persons who are qualified to become 
directors of the Company and who may be appointed 
in senior management in accordance with the 
criteria laid down, and recommend to the Board their 
appointment and removal. The Company shall disclose 
the remuneration policy and the evaluation criteria in 
its annual report;
 (f) Analysing, monitoring and reviewing various human 
resource and compensation matters;
 (g) Determining the Company’s policy on specific 
remuneration packages for executive directors 
including pension rights and any compensation 
payment, and determining remuneration packages of 
such directors;
 (h) Recommending the remuneration, in whatever form, 
payable to the senior management personnel and 
other staff (as deemed necessary);
 (i) Reviewing and approving compensation strategy from 
time to time in the context of the then current Indian 
market in accordance with a pplicable laws;
 (j) Determining whether to extend or continue the term 
of appointment of the independent director, on the 
basis of the report of performance evaluation of 
independent directors;
 (k) Perform such functions as are required to be performed 
by the compensation committee under the Securities 
and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee 
Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021;
 (l) Administering, monitoring and formulating the 
employee stock option scheme/plan approved by the 
Board and shareholders of the Company in accordance 
with the applicable laws (“ESOP Scheme”) 
  (i) Determining the eligibility of employees to 
participate under the ESOP Scheme;
  (ii) Determining the quantum of option to be 
granted under the ESOP Scheme per employee 
and in aggregate; 
  (iii) Date of grant;
  (iv) Determining the exercise price of the option under 
the ESOP Scheme;
  (v) The conditions under which option may vest in 
employee and may lapse in case of termination of 
employment for misconduct;
  (vi) The exercise period within which the employee 
should exercise the option and that option would 
lapse on failure to exercise the option within the 
exercise period;
  (vii) The specified time period within which the 
employee shall exercise the vested option in the 
event of termination or resignation of an employee;
180
Annual Report 2025-26

  (viii) The right of an employee to exercise all the options 
vested in him at one time or at various points of 
time within the e xercise period;
  (ix) Re-pricing of the options which are not exercised, 
whether or not they have been vested if stock 
option rendered unattractive due to fall in the 
market price of the equity shares;
  (x) The grant, vest and exercise of option in case of 
employees who are on long leave;
  (xi) Allow exercise of unvested options on such terms 
and conditions as it may deem fit;
  (xii) The procedure for cashless exercise of options;
  (xiii) Forfeiture/ cancellation of options granted;
  (xiv) Formulating and implementing the procedure for 
making a fair and reasonable adjustment to the 
number of options and to the exercise price in case 
of corporate actions such as rights issues, bonus 
issues, merger, sale of division and others. In this 
regard following shall be taken into consideration:
   a) the number and the price of stock option 
shall be adjusted in a manner such that total 
value of the option to the employee remains 
the same after the corporate action;
   b) for this purpose, global best practices in this 
area including the procedures followed by 
the derivative markets in India and abroad 
may be considered; and
   c) the vesting period and the life of the option 
shall be left unaltered as far as possible to 
protect the rights of the employee who is 
grante d such option. 
 (m) Construing and interpreting the ESOP Scheme and 
any agreements defining the rights and obligations of 
the Company and eligible employees under the ESOP 
Scheme, and prescribing, amending and/or rescinding 
rules and regulations relating to the administration of 
the ESOP Scheme; (n) Framing suitable policies, procedures and systems to 
ensure that there is no violation of securities laws, as 
amended from time to time, including:
  (a) the Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 
2015, as amended; 
  (b) the Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade 
Practices Relating to the Securities Market) 
Regulations, 2003, as amended; and 
  (c) SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended by 
the Company and its employees,  as applicable;
 (o) Performing such other activities as may be delegated 
by the Board and/or are statutorily prescribed under 
any law to be attended to by the Nomination and 
Remunera tion Committee;
 (p) Such terms of reference as may be prescribed under 
the Companies Act and SEBI Listing Regulations and 
other applicable laws.  
 The Committee effectively discharged its roles and 
responsibilities during the year in accordance with its 
terms of reference.

 iv. Review of the various measures and initiatives taken by

dividends and ensuring timely receipt of dividend 
warrants/annual reports/statutory notices by the 
shareholders of the Company.

6. RISK MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE
(A) BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF TERMS OF REFERENCE 
 The Role and Terms of Reference of Risk Management 
Committee (“RM Committee”) are in accordance with the 
requirements of Regulation 21 of the Listing Regulations read 
with Part D of Schedule II of the Listing Regulations.
 The RM Committee is responsible for overseeing the 
Company’s risk management framework and ensuring 
effective identification, assessment and mitigation of 
risks. The brief terms of reference of the Committee 
are set out below:
 (i) To formulate a detailed risk management policy 
which shall include:
	 framework for identification of internal and 
external risks specifically faced by the Company, 
in particular including financial, operational, 
sectoral, sustainability (particularly, Environmental, 
Social and Governance (ESG) related risks), 
information, cyber security risks or any other risk 
as may be determined;	 Measures for risk mitigation including 
systems and processes for internal control of 
identi fied risks; and
	 Business c ontinuity plan.
 (ii) To ensure that appropriate methodology, processes 
and systems are in place to monitor and evaluate risks 
associated with the business of the Company;
 (iii) To monitor and oversee implementation of the risk 
management policy, including evaluating the adequacy 
of risk mana gement systems;
 (iv) To periodically review the risk management policy, at 
least once in two years, including by considering the 
changing industry dynamics and evolv ing complexity;
 (v) To keep the board of directors informed about the 
nature and content of its discussions, recommendations 
and actions to be taken;
 (vi) The appointment, removal and terms of remuneration 
of the Chief Risk Officer shall be subject to review by the 
Risk Management Committee;
 (vii) To seek information from any employee, obtain 
outside legal or other professional advice and secure 
attendance of outsiders with relevant expertise, if it 
considers necessary;
 (viii) Laying down risk assessment and minimization 
procedures and the procedures to inform 
Board of the same;
 (ix) Framing, implementing, reviewing and monitoring the 
risk management plan for the Company and such 
other functions, including cyber security, as may be 
delegated by the Board; and
 (x) Performing such other activities as may be delegated 
by the Board and/or are statutorily prescribed 
under any law to be attended to by the Risk 
Management Committee.
 The Committee effectively discharged its roles and 
responsibilities during the year in accordance with its 
terms of reference.

 (iv) Procedure for Postal Ballot
  The postal ballot is conducted in accordance with the 
provisions contained in Section 110 and other applicable 
provisions, if any, of the Companies Act, 2013, read with 
Rules 20 and 22 of the Companies (Management and 
Administration) Rules, 2014. The postal ballot notice is 
sent to shareholders as per the permitted mode. The 
Company also publishes a notice in the newspapers 
in accordance with the requirements under the 
Compa nies Act, 2013.
  The Shareholders are provided the facility to vote. 
Shareholders holding equity shares as on the cut-off 
date may cast their votes through e-voting during the 
voting period fixed for this purpose. After completion 
of scrutiny of votes, the scrutinizer submits report to 
the Chairman and the results of voting by postal ballot 
are announced within 2 working days of conclusion of the voting period. The results are displayed on the 
website of the Company; https://www.inoxgreen.com/; 
and communicated to the Stock Exchanges where the 
equity shares of the Company are listed and E-voting 
Service Provider. The resolutions, if passed by the 
requisite majority, are deemed to have been passed on 
the last date specifie d for e-voting.

 11.9 Securities Transfer System
  Pursuant to Regulation 40 of the SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015, requests for transfer of securities are processed 
only when the securities are held in dematerialised form with the depositories, namely National Securities 
Depository Limited (NSDL) and Central Depository 
Services (India) Limited (CDSL).
  As on 31st March, 2026, 100% of the Company's paid-
up equity share capital was held in dematerialised form. 
Consequently, no requests for transfer or transmission 
of shares in physical form were received during FY 
2025-26. Transfers of equity shares held in electronic 
form are effected through the depositories through the 
respective Depository Participants (DPs) and do not 
require any involvement of the Company.
  In accordance with applicable SEBI regulations 
and circulars, investor service requests such as 
transmission, transposition, issue of duplicate securities 
certificates, consolidation/splitting of securities 
certificates and other prescribed service requests are 
processed only in demat erialised form.
  The Company, in coordination with its Registrar and 
Share Transfer Agent (RTA), maintains adequate systems 
and procedures to facilitate efficient investor services 
and ensure timely redressal of shareholder grievances.

  c. A brief on types of customers
   The Company is a leading provider of comprehensive long-term Operations and Maintenance (O&M) services for wind 
energy assets, delivering end-to-end solutions that ensure the efficient, reliable, and sustainable operation of wind farms 
throughout their lifecycle. Its service portfolio is designed to optimize the performance, availability, and longevity of wind 
power projects by combining technical expertise, advanced monitoring capabilities, and proactive maintenance practices.
   The Company caters to a diverse range of customers, including Independent Power Producers (IPPs), Public Sector 
Power Utilities, corporate entities, commercial establishments, and retail energy consumers. Leveraging its extensive 
industry experience and technical capabilities, the Company provides customized O&M solutions that address the unique 
operational requirements of each client while ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory and sa fety standards.
   The Company's O&M services encompass preventive and predictive maintenance, corrective maintenance, condition 
monitoring, remote asset surveillance, fault diagnosis, breakdown management, spare parts planning, performance 
optimization, and site management. Through continuous real-time monitoring and data-driven decision-making, the 
Company identifies potential operational issues at an early stage, enabling timely interventions that minimize equipment 
failures and unplanned downtime.
   By adopting a proactive and technology-driven maintenance approach, the Company helps clients maximize energy 
generation, improve turbine availability, enhance operational efficiency, reduce lifecycle maintenance costs, and extend 
the useful life of wind energy assets. Its unwavering commitment to operational excellence, safety, quality, and customer 
satisfaction enables clients to achieve higher plant performance, improved return on investment, and long-term value 
creation from their renewable energy infrastructure.

established, reducing dependency 
on external vendors. For critical

corrective actions to minimize 
failures. For example, failures of

same are not met.The Company’s commitment to sustainability is embedded in its business strategy and is 
reflected in its comprehensive portfolio of customized solutions designed to address the 
evolving needs of its customers and the renewable energy sector. By delivering reliable, 
efficient, and value-driven services, the Company contributes to the advancement of 
clean energy infrastructure while creating long-term value for its stakeholders.
With a strong focus on the long-term Operations and Maintenance (O&M) of Wind Turbine 
Generators (WTGs) and their associated infrastructure, the Company provides end-to-end 
solutions aimed at ensuring the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of wind energy assets 
throughout their lifecycle. Its services include preventive and predictive maintenance, 
condition monitoring, performance optimization, fault diagnosis, and timely corrective 
interventions, enabling uninterrupted operations and minimizing equipment downtime.
Through its technical expertise, advanced monitoring capabilities, and proactive 
maintenance practices, the Company helps customers maximize turbine availability, 
improve energy generation efficiency, reduce lifecycle maintenance costs, and extend 
the operational life of their renewable energy assets. By enhancing the performance and 
reliability of wind power infrastructure, the Company actively supports the transition to 
clean energy, promotes resource efficiency, and contributes to the development of a low-
carbon and more sustainable future.

2. Does the entity have processes in place to avoid/ manage conflict of interests involving members of the Board? (Yes/No) If Yes,

 Yes. In accordance with the Companies Act, 2013, Directors are required to annually disclose their interests and any relationships 
that may give rise to an actual or potential conflict of interest. Based on these disclosures, the Company maintains a statutory 
register to ensure transparency and facilitate the effective management of potential conflicts. Directors who have an interest in 
any matter are required to disclose such interest and abstain from participating in discussions and voting on the relevant agenda

10. Health and safety management system:
 a. Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? 
  Yes, Occupational health and safety management system has been implemented as per ISO 45001:2018 and certified. It 
covers the entire operations. The Company has instituted a robust Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Management System 
designed to safeguard the health, safety and well-being of all employees and stakeholders. This system is governed by a 
comprehensive HSE Policy, which articulates the Company's commitment to: Providing a safe, secure and healthy workplace 
Identifying and mitigating occupational hazards Complying with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements Encouraging 
continuous improvement in safety performance Integrating environmental and safety consciousness into operational practices 
The coverage of the HSE Management System spans all service locations and operational areas where the Company provides 
Operation and Maintenance (O&M) services for Wind Turbine Generators (WTGs) and related infrastructure. The Company 
actively promotes a safety-first culture across its workforce and partners, aiming to prevent incidents and promote sustainable 
environmental practices.
